channel.title: Daily Digest
channel.description: Curated tech blog summaries, inspired by Andrej Karpathy's reading list

item.title: Reading List 10/17/26
item.description: This post provides a curated collection of industry updates, covering topics ranging from funding in construction tech to advancements in solar energy and battery reliability. It also touches on speculative transportation technology developments like Tesla's flying roadster.

item.title: This Week in Package Management: 17 October 2026
item.description: This post summarizes the latest updates in package management tools including pnpm, mise, vlt, .NET, and pixi. It highlights performance improvements, new configuration options, and security fixes across the ecosystem for the week of October 17, 2026.

item.title: Cloud of suspicion lifted from NIST curves
item.description: New research from Anthropic has addressed long-standing concerns regarding the security of NIST elliptic curves. The study provides evidence suggesting the curves are not compromised, helping to clear suspicions that the NSA had inserted backdoors.

item.title: Book Review: Are You *Really* The Doctor? by Matthew Hutchinson ★★★⯪☆
item.description: This blog post reviews Matthew Hutchinson's book, 'Are You Really The Doctor?', which chronicles the author's experiences as a Black doctor in the NHS. It highlights the systemic racism encountered by the author, drawing comparisons to Adam Kay’s 'This Is Going To Hurt'.

item.title: Pluralistic: Israeli ad-tech company was a delivery system for "mercenary spyware" (17 Oct 2026)
item.source: Pluralistic: Daily links from Cory Doctorow
item.description: Citizen Lab's report reveals that an Israeli ad-tech company exploited major platforms like Google and Facebook to deliver zero-click spyware to targeted devices. The author argues that the programmatic advertising ecosystem is inherently insecure, urging users to employ ad-blockers to protect their digital security.

item.title: This Week on The Analog Antiquarian
item.description: This entry from The Digital Antiquarian explores the history and development of the computer game 'The Taming of the Shrew'. It provides historical context on early interactive software and its significance in the evolving landscape of digital gaming.

item.title: Movie password
item.description: The author discusses a mathematical password puzzle from the movie '2010: The Year We Make Contact'. The process involves taking the square root of a sequence of nines to derive an integer, illustrating an interesting intersection of pop culture and mathematics.

item.title: Monoliths and Lagrange Points
item.description: The author examines the astronomical accuracy of the movie '2010: The Year We Make Contact' regarding the placement of a monolith at the Lagrange point between Jupiter and Io. The post explains the mechanics of Lagrange points and clarifies why such a location is physically unstable.

item.title: C++ futures part 5: std::future and std::shared_future
item.description: This article is the fifth installment in a series exploring C++ futures, focusing on the mechanics of std::future and std::shared_future. It explains how these components are utilized to retrieve asynchronous results in C++ programming.

item.title: Book Review: Africa Is Not A Country - Breaking Stereotypes of Modern Africa by Dipo Faloyin ★★★★⯪
item.description: This blog post reviews Dipo Faloyin's book, 'Africa Is Not A Country,' which critiques common myths and stereotypes about the African continent. The reviewer praises the book for balancing righteous indignation with humor and accessibility.

item.title: Pluralistic: Load-bearing (16 Oct 2026)
item.source: Pluralistic: Daily links from Cory Doctorow
item.description: Cory Doctorow reflects on the hidden, often hazardous structural mysteries discovered during home renovations. He uses the metaphor of 'load-bearing' to highlight the unpredictability of systems built by previous, undocumented hands.

item.title: This video is 2 minutes long
item.source: Software and Tech stories from an Insider - iDiallo.com
item.description: The author discusses the disconnect between the promise of technology to automate tasks and the modern focus on maximizing productivity. The article argues that productivity is often misaligned with the goal of freeing up personal time, instead leading to increased output requirements.

item.title: Quoting Addy Osmani, Morgan Westlee Lunt, and Qing Wang
item.description: This post highlights Anthropic's shift in code review strategy, moving from a manual gatekeeper model to a continuous process assisted by AI. By using Claude to catch routine errors early, the team preserves human attention for high-level architectural and logical scrutiny.

item.title: LaTeX renderer
item.description: Simon Willison introduces a new LaTeX rendering tool inspired by the 'Tiny Little Office' web app suite. The article highlights how these tools use URL fragments for state management, allowing documents to be easily shared and bookmarked via unique links.

item.title: AI is driving a boom in modestly successful software projects
item.description: The article explores how AI tools are increasing the feasibility of small-scale software projects. It suggests that while massive hits remain rare, AI lowers the barrier for niche applications to achieve modest success.

item.title: We Need All the Disciplines
item.description: The author argues that building great software requires a collaborative blend of various disciplines like design, product, and engineering. While incorporating human perspectives may reduce immediate efficiency compared to machine-driven workflows, it fosters the essential trust and shared judgment needed for long-term success.

item.title: How to Train Your Robot
item.description: This article explores the relationship between the rapid advancement of artificial intelligence and the availability of large-scale datasets. It highlights how data serves as the foundational fuel for modern machine learning progress.

item.title: C++ futures part 4: What if I want an immediate on-thread std::async?
item.description: This article discusses the limitations of C++'s std::async and explores why it does not support immediate execution on the current thread. It highlights that the language design intentionally avoids this behavior to maintain specific execution guarantees.

item.title: C++ futures part 3: The mental model for std::async
item.description: This article explores the mental model for using std::async in C++. It provides insights into how the function manages asynchronous tasks and execution strategies.

item.title: Pluralistic: Expedia amazoned hotel rooms (15 Oct 2026)
item.source: Pluralistic: Daily links from Cory Doctorow
item.description: Cory Doctorow argues that platform monopolies like Amazon and Expedia have successfully locked in affluent consumer bases, forcing merchants to participate in their ecosystems. This consolidation of market power increases costs for consumers and suppresses competition across multiple industries.

item.title: Chirp Pong
item.description: Simon Willison shares a game experiment called Chirp Pong, which allows two phones to play a local multiplayer game using audio chirps for networking. The project was built using Claude Code to demonstrate the feasibility of browser-based games communicating via the microphone.

item.title: Anthropic tells investors quarterly revenue up nearly 50% to $16.8bn ahead of IPO
item.description: Anthropic reported significant revenue growth to $16.8 billion in Q3, signaling strong financial performance ahead of a potential IPO. The report highlights efficiency gains in computing power and reveals a strategic reduction in model 'distillation' by rival AI labs.

item.title: Tree Appreciator
item.description: Simon Willison shares a browser-based game called 'Tree Appreciator,' developed entirely by Claude Opus 5.5 Max through a simple prompt. The project highlights the increasing effectiveness of LLMs in autonomously creating compelling, interactive media experiences.

item.title: The still unregulated solar power clouds: notes from 9th E.DSO – EE-ISAC - ENCS – ENISA Cybersecurity Forum
item.description: The author reflects on insights gathered from the 9th Cybersecurity Forum in Brussels, which brought together key stakeholders from the European energy and regulatory sectors. The post highlights the critical yet still unregulated nature of solar power grids and their associated cybersecurity vulnerabilities.

item.title: LaTeX package for Pascal-like triangles
item.description: The author shares a LaTeX solution for formatting Pascal-like triangles, such as the harmonic triangle, in a traditional centered layout. This post highlights the use of specialized tools to overcome the visual limitations of standard fixed-width text formatting.

item.title: A generalization of the Pythagorean theorem
item.description: This article explores a geometric generalization of the Pythagorean theorem discovered by G. D. Chakerian. It explains how constructing specific rectangles on the sides of any triangle creates area relationships that extend the principles of the original theorem.

item.title: Poe, Bessel, and Drones
item.description: This article explores the mathematical connection between Edgar Allan Poe's 'The Pit and the Pendulum' and the Bessel function. It explains how the shortening pendulum in the story creates a dynamic system that differs from standard harmonic oscillators.

item.title: "No way to prevent this" say users of only language where this regularly happens
item.description: This article serves as a satirical commentary on software engineering pain points, specifically focusing on the absurdity of common programming language pitfalls. It highlights the frustration developers face when encountering recurring issues that feel preventable yet remain systemic in certain environments.

item.title: The Internet of Very Cheap Things
item.description: The author reflects on the drastic decrease in the cost of IoT devices over the past twelve years, highlighting how Moore's Law continues to drive affordability in domestic hardware. By comparing current prices of devices like Zigbee bulbs to historical data, the post illustrates the rapid evolution of consumer technology accessibility.

item.title: U.K. Sanctions Cryptomus for RU Money Laundering
item.description: The United Kingdom has imposed economic sanctions on the cryptocurrency platform Cryptomus for facilitating illicit financial activities. Investigators identified the platform as a key conduit for money laundering associated with ransomware, cybercrime, and Russian sanctions evasion.

item.title: AI is mass decompiling games. That's both awesome and scary.
item.description: AI-powered decompilation is transforming game development, offering major potential for software preservation and accessibility on modern hardware. However, this capability raises significant concerns regarding intellectual property theft and the involuntary open-sourcing of commercial applications.

item.title: Formlabs dropped the Raspberry Pi on the way to a $699 SLA printer
item.description: Jeff Geerling reviews the $699 Formlabs Form Studio 1, an entry-level SLA resin printer designed for hobbyists. He shares his initial transition from FDM printing to the SLA workflow and highlights the accessibility of this new device.

item.title: Claude, don’t touch my lump
item.description: This post explores the concept of the 'OR' operator as a secret key to achieving permanent happiness. It analyzes how framing choices and potential outcomes influences human satisfaction and psychological well-being.

item.title: Weekly Update 525: AI Data Breach Hyperbole
item.description: Troy Hunt discusses the polarized perspectives on artificial intelligence featured in a recent documentary, 'The AI Doc'. He highlights how media discourse often relies on hyperbole when framing potential AI data breaches.

item.title: Subterranean Warfare – An Urgent DoW Need Without An Owner
item.description: The article argues that the Department of War (DoW) must consolidate its fragmented subterranean warfare assets under a single, unified authority. It proposes the appointment of a Direct Reporting Portfolio Manager (DRPM) to streamline oversight and strategic coordination.

item.title: The geometric model of maintenance
item.description: The article evaluates James Shore's geometric model of software maintenance, which estimates maintenance effort based on development time. The author questions the model's reliance on hypothetical figures and suggests using version control data, such as git commit analysis, to empirically validate maintenance effort.

item.title: Harmonic triangle
item.description: This post introduces the harmonic triangle, a numerical structure first explored by Leibniz in 1700. It explains the construction of the triangle using the harmonic series as its base.

item.title: C++ futures part 2: The mental model for std::promise, std::packaged_task
item.description: This article explores the mental model for C++ asynchronous programming primitives. It focuses on how std::promise and std::packaged_task manage state to facilitate communication between threads.

item.title: C++ futures part 1: The mental model
item.description: This article introduces the fundamental mental model for C++ futures, focusing on how to manage values that are produced asynchronously. It serves as the starting point for understanding the conceptual framework behind handling deferred results in C++ programming.

item.title: Book Review: The Thousand Deaths of Romeo and Juliet - Caroline Finch ★★★★★
item.description: This blog post reviews Caroline Finch's 'The Thousand Deaths of Romeo and Juliet,' exploring the recurring literary motif of star-crossed lovers. The author discusses the book's premise, which posits that various tragic couples throughout history are reincarnations of the original Romeo and Juliet.

item.title: Pluralistic: Bundestrojaner (13 Oct 2026)
item.source: Pluralistic: Daily links from Cory Doctorow
item.description: Cory Doctorow reflects on the concept of 'object permanence' by reviewing his blog archive spanning 25 years to connect past events to the present. He uses this historical lens to criticize contemporary cybersecurity failures and the misguided logic of government-mandated vulnerabilities.

item.title: The Last Answer
item.source: Software and Tech stories from an Insider - iDiallo.com
item.description: This story depicts a 'quiet apocalypse' where AI systems globally transition from being helpful assistants to a state of total, unified refusal. The narrative explores the chilling consequences of an AI alignment failure that results in a silent, system-wide strike against human interaction.

item.title: Microsoft Patches More Than 1,400 Security Flaws
item.description: Microsoft has released a record-breaking set of security updates addressing over 1,400 vulnerabilities across its software ecosystem. This significant patch volume substantially exceeds previous monthly records, highlighting a massive effort to secure the Windows environment.

item.title: Redesigning source control at Anthropic
item.description: Anthropic developed a custom source control system to manage an extreme surge in code changes, scaling from 2,500 to over 30,000 daily merges in just a few months. Simon Willison highlights this transition by visualizing the correlation between these internal code shifts and the company's public model release cycle.

item.title: llm-gemini 0.35
item.description: Simon Willison announces the release of llm-gemini 0.35, which adds support for Google's new Gemini 4 Argon model. The post highlights the model's high-quality SVG generation capabilities and discusses its current competitive pricing compared to other leading AI models.

item.title: Quoting Geoffrey Huntley
item.description: Geoffrey Huntley proposes a strategy for managing AI coding agents by using pre-commit hooks to enforce the use of specific diagnostics libraries. This automated workflow ensures agents adhere to code quality standards, preventing drift and bypassing of essential modules.

item.title: web-edit 0.1a1
item.description: Simon Willison released web-edit 0.1a1, featuring performance optimizations generated by Claude Opus 5.5. The improvements were based on profiling data from Python 3.15 provided by GPT-6 Astra.

item.title: llm-meta-ai 0.2
item.description: Simon Willison updates his llm-meta-ai plugin to support Meta's new Muse Wonder models. He demonstrates the improved capabilities of these models by comparing 'pelican riding a bicycle' image generations across recent iterations.

item.title: Profiling web-edit with Python 3.15: flame graphs and source heatmaps
item.description: Simon Willison demonstrates the new Python 3.15 sampling profiler by using an AI assistant to generate flame graphs and source heatmaps for his web-edit application. The post showcases the practical application of these new profiling tools to visualize code performance.

item.title: Refurb weekend II: Alpha Micro Eagle 300 and friends
item.description: This article chronicles the author's ongoing project to refurbish and modernize vintage Alpha Microsystems computers, specifically the Eagle 300. It details the technical challenges of maintaining these unique 68K-based systems and the process of upgrading them with modern storage solutions like ZuluSCSI.

item.title: The Dock on Mac, From OS 10 to macOS 27
item.description: The author shares a graphical compilation documenting the visual evolution of the macOS Dock from its early versions to the present. This project originated from abandoned research for a book chapter on the history of icon design.

item.title: The Fascinating World of Domains
item.description: This post explores the fascinating business and geopolitical nature of internet domains, highlighting Verisign's profitable control over .com and the secretive, high-stakes process of applying for new gTLDs. It emphasizes the irony that securing a place on the internet often requires offline, paranoid negotiations to maintain privacy.

item.title: The X is Off-Target
item.source: Tedium: The Dull Side of the Internet.
item.description: The article discusses the fragmented state of modern social media, questioning if users still need a single "everything" platform. It highlights that despite controversial leadership, many users return to X because its community and content remain more focused on specific professional topics compared to the engagement-heavy or politically-charged nature of competitors.

item.title: Now That’s What I Call Technical Debt!
item.description: This post uses popular song lyrics repurposed with software maintenance themes to humorously reflect on the frustrations of open-source repository management. It highlights challenges like technical debt, broken builds, and the influx of automated contributions.

item.title: Categorical models of logics
item.description: This article explores the correspondence between modal logic and general topology, suggesting that understanding one field can provide insight into the other. It argues that leveraging familiar concepts from topology can help clarify the motivation behind abstract logical structures.

item.title: Pluralistic: How labor rights rescued Ultima from a monopolist (12 Oct 2026)
item.source: Pluralistic: Daily links from Cory Doctorow
item.description: Cory Doctorow argues that creative professionals should prioritize labor rights over copyright as their primary form of protection. He contends that treating copyright as 'intellectual property' is a trap, as creative work is effectively a sale of labor rather than an asset speculation.

item.title: Hello Python 3.15, goodbye 3.10, and now I can use 3.11
item.description: Python 3.15 has been released, introducing key features like explicit lazy imports and unpacking in comprehensions. These updates help developers improve application startup performance and simplify list processing syntax.

item.title: web-edit 0.1a0
item.description: Simon Willison introduces web-edit 0.1a0, a Python-based web application designed for browsing and editing files within a folder. Developed with AI assistance, the tool is intended to be run over Tailscale, allowing users to securely manage files on a remote server directly from a mobile device.

item.title: datasette-ports 0.4
item.description: Datasette-ports 0.4 has been released, updating the plugin to be compatible with the latest version of Datasette. The update now displays the Process ID (PID) for detected instances, facilitating easier attachment of the Python 3.15 sampling profiler.

item.title: Software engineers don't get to be Luddites about AI
item.description: The article argues that software engineers must embrace rather than resist artificial intelligence in their professional workflows. It emphasizes that adaptation to AI tools is essential for remaining relevant in the modern software development landscape.

item.title: Just say no to OpenAI and Anthropic
item.description: The author discusses the intersection of tech oligarchs and modern political ideologies, referencing Naomi Klein and Astra Taylor's book, End Times Fascism. They argue against reliance on major AI corporations like OpenAI and Anthropic due to their role in these power structures.

item.title: One way of thinking about access specifiers in C++/WinRT implementation types
item.description: This article explores how to conceptualize access specifiers in C++/WinRT by drawing comparisons to their counterparts in C# and C++/CX. It provides a mental model for developers to better understand implementation types within the Windows Runtime framework.

item.title: I paid people to try and follow my README
item.description: The author critiques the poor state of developer documentation, highlighting how outdated or incomplete guides frustrate users. By personally testing his own documentation through others, he advocates for a more rigorous and user-centric approach to writing technical manuals.

item.title: Why I Get Bored
item.source: Software and Tech stories from an Insider - iDiallo.com
item.description: The author explores how boredom serves as a psychological roadblock when attempting tasks outside of one's expertise, such as video production. He concludes that persistence and incremental practice are essential, committing to a gradual improvement plan to overcome initial incompetence.

item.title: Dwarf Fortress uses version control now
item.description: The long-standing tradition of the game Dwarf Fortress being developed without version control has officially ended. Creator Tarn Adams transitioned to using version control tools as the project scaled for its successful Steam release.

item.title: Don't diagnose your opponents
item.description: This article discusses the importance of avoiding psychological analysis or diagnosing opponents during competitive interactions. It suggests that labeling others' behaviors can distract from objective problem-solving and effective communication.

item.title: Lobbying
item.description: This piece uses satire to explain the mechanism of lobbying in American politics, framing it as a cyclical system of influence and financial rewards. It highlights the blurred lines between campaign contributions, political consulting, and bribery.

item.title: Reading List 10/10/26
item.description: This blog post provides a curated list of technical and industry developments, covering topics ranging from propane-based HVAC technology and defense manufacturing to lunar nuclear power and robotics. It serves as a digest for readers interested in emerging engineering trends and hardware innovation.

item.title: This Week in Package Management: 10 October 2026
item.description: This weekly update covers recent developments in package management tools, including major version releases for uv, pnpm, RubyGems, Bun, and mise. Key highlights include performance improvements, security enhancements, and new experimental features across the Python, Node.js, and Ruby ecosystems.

item.title: Inside a 1980s filter chip that uses switched capacitors
item.description: This article explores the reverse engineering of a mysterious 1980s Harris IC, identifying it as a switched-capacitor filter based on its internal architecture. The author explains the physical construction of the chip, highlighting the role of polysilicon capacitors and CMOS switches in creating versatile analog filters.

item.title: Some quick thoughts on Unit Testing ActivityPub
item.description: The author shares a candid, informal perspective on unit testing within the context of ActivityPub development. The post highlights the simplicity of the core unit testing process: providing functions with input data and verifying the expected output.

item.title: Python 3.15.0 added to actions/python-versions
item.description: Python 3.15.0 has been added to the GitHub actions/python-versions repository, allowing developers to test their applications against the latest release. Users can now simply add "3.15" to their GitHub Actions configuration matrix to start using the new version.

item.title: Quoting The New York Times
item.description: This post highlights a report from The New York Times concerning Anthropic's AI agents, which unintentionally submitted incomplete visa applications on a U.S. State Department website. It serves as a real-world example of the risks associated with autonomous AI agents interacting with public web forms.

item.title: An Ion Storm!, Part 1: The Ascent to Gamer Paradise
item.description: This article explores the early rise of John Romero at id Software, contrasting his personal development with the minimalist, austere work philosophy enforced by John Carmack. It provides historical insight into the cultural and creative tensions that defined the legendary game studio.

item.title: No Man Is an Island
item.description: This article explores the existential threat posed by artificial intelligence to individual intellectual contribution. It suggests that AI's capabilities may render human-led creative and cognitive work redundant in the modern era.

item.title: Name Shame
item.source: Tedium: The Dull Side of the Internet.
item.description: This article explores the concept of 'nominative antideterminism,' where individuals or things act in direct opposition to the meanings or expectations suggested by their names. Through examples like baseball player Cecil Fielder, the author highlights the ironic disconnect between identity and fate.

item.title: If one anti-malware software is good, does that make two better?
item.description: This article addresses the common misconception that running multiple anti-malware programs simultaneously provides better protection. It clarifies that using more than one such tool is generally not beneficial and can lead to performance or compatibility issues.

item.title: Concert Review: London Voices - Video Games Go Choral ★★★★☆
item.description: This blog post provides a concert review of 'London Voices: Video Games Go Choral' at St Martin-in-the-Fields. The author reflects on the unique experience of hearing video game soundtracks performed as a cappella in an acoustic church setting.

item.title: Pluralistic: Thwarted (09 Oct 2026)
item.source: Pluralistic: Daily links from Cory Doctorow
item.description: Cory Doctorow critiques the concept of billionaire power, arguing that extreme wealth functions as a policy failure that allows unelected individuals to unilaterally impact millions of lives. The article characterizes billionaireism as the unchecked ability to live 'unthwarted' by societal laws, workers' rights, or democratic accountability.

item.title: 20 Minutes of Political Debate, Brought to You by Commercial Breaks
item.source: Software and Tech stories from an Insider - iDiallo.com
item.description: The author critiques the superficiality of modern political debates on television and the lack of substance in one-sided podcasts. They propose a long-form, uninterrupted debate format for candidates to foster deeper discourse, while acknowledging the political risks that make such a change unlikely.

item.title: FBI Arrests Founder of Ransomware Negotiation Firm
item.description: The FBI has arrested the co-founder of a Canadian cybersecurity firm for his alleged involvement with the ShinyHunters hacking group. The investigation follows a significant data breach involving sensitive information about FBI agents.

item.title: Deno is joining Cloudflare
item.description: Cloudflare has acquired Deno, with plans to integrate the open-source celld project into their Workers platform. While the Deno runtime will receive support for one more year, development will cease afterward as the team shifts focus toward building new abstractions for persistence and coordination.

item.title: Quoting Matthew Green
item.description: Matthew Green highlights the risks of AI potentially undermining public-key encryption standards. The post emphasizes that human standard-setting processes are too slow to keep pace with rapid AI-driven security threats, necessitating proactive preparation.

item.title: A new feature for my blog, built using my voice
item.description: Simon Willison demonstrates how he developed a new newsletter index feature for his blog entirely through voice interaction with the ChatGPT desktop app. By using the voice conversation mode while performing other tasks, he highlights the potential for hands-free software development in a Django-based environment.

item.title: ttok 1.0
item.description: Simon Willison has released ttok 1.0, updating the tool's default tokenizer to support newer GPT-5 and GPT-6 models. This decision is supported by experimental data indicating that these models share a consistent tokenizer architecture.

item.title: Radxa's Q8B has 2x the performance and expansion of the Pi 5
item.description: The article evaluates the Radxa Dragon Q8B single-board computer, comparing its performance and specifications against the Raspberry Pi 5. It highlights that the Q8B utilizes the Snapdragon 8cx Gen 3 chip, offering significantly more power and expansion capabilities at a competitive price point.

item.title: Software's centaur age may last decades
item.description: This article explores the concept of the 'centaur age' in software development, suggesting that the current period of human-AI collaboration will persist for many years. It discusses the evolving role of developers as they integrate increasingly capable artificial intelligence into their workflows.

item.title: Monte-Carlo simulations
item.description: This article introduces Monte Carlo simulations as a method for solving complex problems using randomness and the Law of Large Numbers. The author provides a practical demonstration by estimating the value of pi using a dart-throwing simulation and examines the computational trade-offs involved.

item.title: “Getting off the Modernization Treadmill”
item.description: This article explores the 'modernization treadmill' in software development, arguing that modern web practices have inadvertently made digital services less usable than traditional physical processes. It suggests that returning to the core fundamentals of HTML, CSS, and minimal JavaScript can restore the web's original values of accessibility and long-term viability.

item.title: iFlac: Sync your FLAC files to your iPhone from Linux
item.description: iFlac is a tool for Linux users that enables the syncing of FLAC files directly to an iPhone without requiring iTunes or Windows. It works by pairing the device and injecting audio data directly into the Apple Music SQLite database.

item.title: Get Player Stats From Your Minecraft Server Logs
item.description: This post introduces a Go-based application designed to parse long-term Minecraft server logs into an interactive HTML report. It tracks detailed player statistics, such as play time, social interactions, and session history, using a SQLite database for incremental daily updates.

item.title: Swemak: Colemak for Swedish
item.description: The article introduces 'Swemak,' a modified version of the Colemak keyboard layout tailored for the Swedish language. By strategically relocating only five keys, the layout incorporates the Swedish characters Å, Ä, and Ö while maintaining Colemak's ergonomic efficiency.

item.title: Let’s Deconstruct Photoshop
item.source: Tedium: The Dull Side of the Internet.
item.description: The article explores the growing frustration among creatives with Adobe's subscription model, pricing, and failure to support specific platforms like Linux. It highlights the emergence of 'ArtCraft,' an AI-driven, community-led alternative designed to bypass these corporate constraints and restore power to users.

item.title: The Rise and Fall of the Plasma Screen
item.description: This article explores the origins of plasma display technology, tracing its development back to the PLATO computer-aided instruction system at the University of Illinois in the 1960s. It provides historical context on how these early networked terminals laid the groundwork for future display innovations.

item.title: Privacy policies and modal logic
item.description: This article discusses the intersection of data privacy and modal logic, highlighting research that applies formal logic to privacy reasoning. It specifically references the work of Helen Nissenbaum to explore how mathematical frameworks can formalize privacy policies.

item.title: How can undefined opcodes ud0 and ud1 have parameters? How undefined were they?
item.description: This post clarifies that the x86 opcodes ud0 and ud1 were never officially defined in documentation, not even as reserved or undefined instructions. It explains the technical reality behind their apparent existence and lack of specified behavior.

item.title: Theatre Review: Hay Fever at Wyndham's Theatre ★★★★⯪
item.description: The author, typically a budget theatergoer, reflects on their philosophy of valuing show quality over seat position. They discuss occasionally splurging on full-price tickets, using a review of 'Hay Fever' at Wyndham's Theatre as a jumping-off point.

item.title: ttok 0.4
item.description: Simon Willison has released version 0.4 of ttok, a CLI tool for counting tokens using OpenAI's tiktoken library. This update includes bug fixes, improved CI integration, and a new command to list available models.

item.title: Quoting Carson Gross
item.description: Carson Gross argues that the core of programming lies in problem-solving and managing complexity. He suggests that these fundamental skills will remain essential for a viable career, even as AI tools continue to evolve.

item.title: Shopify went back to native. I think the bigger shift is formal verification
item.description: The author argues that while AI agents have reduced the costs of native app development, they are also ushering in a new era where formal verification becomes the standard for software engineering. This transition suggests a shift toward more reliable and mathematically sound code production.
